selection_rule: Registered publishers (IEA, LBNL, EPRI, McKinsey, Goldman Sachs, BloombergNEF, S&P Global with 451 Research, Deloitte and Gartner) were searched on 9 October 2026 for publications dated after the 8 October 2026 currency sweep. Two editions from other publishers were added at the author's decision of 9 October 2026: TrendForce's press release of 16 September 2026 and AEMO's 2026 data-centre forecast with Oxford Economics Australia, published in August 2026. A figure is registered only where the publisher's own retained publication states a value with a target year, unit and geography that the ledger's fields can hold; a financial-year target is recorded under the source's own year label, with the financial-year basis stated. Other values in the same publications are listed as known unregistered values. Candidates await independent claim-support receipts and enter no arithmetic until a supported receipt is bound. The sample remains a convenience sample of named institutions, not a census. Non-US addition, at the author's request of 11 October 2026, under a rule declared and recorded before the new originals were retrieved: European geographies first, from the registered publishers' European figures and from European public bodies and transmission system operators, then China; a figure only from the forecasting body's own retained publication dated 2025 or 2026 that states a value with a target year, unit and geography the ledger's fields can hold, the 2030 value where one is stated; the base, central, reference or median case, or else the case the publication presents as its headline, with its name; each publisher's own definition of the geography; a figure stated only in another organisation's publication is a lead, not registered. Settled after retrieval, because the rule left them open: a publisher's latest edition is registered and an earlier edition's figure listed as a known unregistered value, because a candidate carries no supersession; where a publication states both annual electricity and capacity for 2030, the annual electricity value is registered, as the ledger does for the IEA; a publication that names no central case but presents two retained trajectories is registered as the range across them, as the ledger records EPRI's scenario range.

records.locator: Press release of 16 September 2026, section on the 2030 global supply-demand capacity gap, second paragraph, first sentence
records.qualification: N01 states the registered value as global data-centre power demand capacity projected for 2030 and divides demand capacity into general servers, AI servers, other IT equipment and non-IT equipment such as cooling and power supply systems, so the boundary includes facility overhead. N01's retained text and its retained article image name no scenario and no data-centre types and do not mention cryptocurrency. TrendForce's 22 September 2026 article (N04) describes the demand line as fleet electricity use converted into power capacity; a note on one of its charts states that TrendForce's line uses a conversion consistent with IEA public data and that LBNL equates its 2030 Reference Case to 148 GW of interconnection capacity at 50% utilisation, and N04's retained text and article images give no number for TrendForce's conversion. No 2030 figure occurs in the retained text or retained article image of TrendForce's earlier release N05, so no earlier TrendForce vintage of this quantity is registered. Other values in N01 are listed as NK01, NK02 and NK10. The underlying report is not retained.
records.method_description: AI server industry research (N01); demand capacity grouped by equipment type, with the non-IT category labelled PUE-derived in the release's chart (N01); shipment estimates accumulated into the fleet in service, whose annual electricity use is converted into power capacity on a basis N04 describes as consistent with IEA public data, with no number given (N04); published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.locator: Table A.4 printed p110 (Europe, total electricity consumption, 2030, Base Case); Annex B printed p122 (definition of Europe)
records.qualification: Europe row of Table A.4: total, as distinct from IT-only, consumption. Annex B defines the IEA's Europe as the European Union regional grouping and Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Gibraltar, Iceland, Israel, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, the Republic of Moldova, Serbia, Switzerland, Türkiye, Ukraine and the United Kingdom, so it is wider than the European Union and is not assumed to match another publisher's Europe. Annex A obtains each region's total by multiplying IT demand by a PUE for each data-centre type. The workbook retained as the IEA's 2025 data annex (N07, whose retrieval record is not held) gives 113 TWh for the same row and year (NK15); only the latest edition is registered, and a one-unit difference between tabulated values is not interpreted as a substantive revision. Other values in N06 are listed as NK11 to NK14. N06 does not state whether its values include cryptocurrency mining. Model projection, not a measured outcome.
records.method_description: Bottom-up model driven by IT equipment shipments, covering servers, storage systems and network equipment inside facilities and excluding data transmission networks; global installed IT capacity allocated to regions mainly from a third-party provider's (IDC's) regional breakdown; total demand obtained by multiplying IT demand by a PUE for each region and data-centre type (Annex A methodology); published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.scenario: décarbonation lente to décarbonation rapide (the two trajectories RTE retained after public consultation)
records.locator: Chapter 2, section 2.5.3 and Figure 2.10 (PDF page 28), data labels at 2030
records.qualification: Electricity consumption of data centres on dedicated sites ('centres de données sur sites dédiés'), a category N08 introduces for the first time, as opposed to in-house data centres in the premises of the organisation that uses them; the 2023 edition counted both (footnote 14). The projections are calibrated to include dedicated-site data centres connected to the distribution network. The values are the 2030 data labels of Figure 2.10: 15 TWh on the line of the décarbonation rapide trajectory and 10 TWh on that of the décarbonation lente trajectory, paired by the colour of label and line; the section's prose states the two trajectories' 2035 levels (NK16) and, outside Figure 2.10, no 2030 level. RTE names no central case: it studies three deliberately contrasting trajectories, décarbonation rapide, built as an update of the 2023 edition's A - référence scenario, décarbonation lente, and a stagnation trajectory studied as a sensitivity test, which for data centres assumes very slow growth to 2030 without a stated value; for data centres it retained the first two after public consultation, and the range spans them. N08's national consumption series are for mainland metropolitan France (Figure 2.1); the data-centre section does not restate its perimeter. N08 does not mention cryptocurrency or state whether the consumption is IT load or includes cooling and other overhead. Other values are listed as NK16 to NK18.
records.method_description: Trajectories built from the power of data-centre projects with a signed connection offer, aggregated by planned connection year, with assumed concretisation rates, a ramp-up of the order of ten years and the maximum power reached: in the décarbonation rapide trajectory, about 60% concretisation (4.3 GW) of transmission-connected projects due before 2030, an average utilisation of 20% of connection capacity at that horizon and about 2.4 TWh of growth from distribution-connected sites; in the décarbonation lente trajectory, about 30% concretisation and about 1.8 TWh of distribution growth (N08 sections 2.5.2 and 2.5.3); published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.scenario: AF25 base course (grundforløb), a target-fulfilment scenario
records.locator: Background note on data centres, section 1.1, page 3 of 9, sentence after the capacity-utilisation assumptions
records.qualification: N09 states that data-centre electricity consumption is assumed to be 6.0 TWh in 2030 ('6,0 TWh i 2030'), from installed capacity for the whole of Denmark assumed at 1,000 MW in 2030 and capacity utilisation that starts at 60% in a data centre's first year of operation and rises to 80% in its fifteenth. AF25 is a target-fulfilment scenario: its base course is in principle compatible with meeting the political climate and energy targets, though not all of them are directly reflected. The included data centres range from about 1 MW to hyperscale sites of 150 MW or more. N09 states that AF25 has markedly lower consumption than AF24 in the short term and higher consumption in the long term. N09 does not mention cryptocurrency or state a facility boundary such as IT load or cooling; its one mention of cooling concerns the Danish climate. Other values are listed as NK19 and NK20.
records.method_description: Projection of data-centre capacity and consumption from Energinet's knowledge of coming data centres, with all installed capacity phased in over ten years, projects in screening weighted at 40% (50% in AF24), capacity growth of just under 2% a year after 2045 and capacity utilisation rising from 60% to 80% over a data centre's first 15 years (N09 sections 1.1 and 1.2 and the list of changes from AF24); published outputs read; model not rebuilt.
